title: Module identity and once-only bodies
prompt:
Implement `class ReloadableModule` demonstrating import-cache semantics:

1. `install(name)` creates a `types.ModuleType(name)`, sets `mod.exec_count = 0`, registers it in `sys.modules[name]`, and stores it on `self.modules[name]`.
2. `import_again(name)` returns `sys.modules[name]` WITHOUT re-executing anything.
3. `simulate_body_execution(name)` increments that module's `exec_count += 1` (simulating a module body run).
4. `identity_stable(name)` returns True when repeated `import_again` calls always return the SAME object.

Graded checks: identity is stable; exec_count only changes when simulate_body_execution is explicitly called — mirroring real import-once semantics.
boilerplate:
import sys
import types

# TODO: ReloadableModule

tests.name: identity is stable, body runs once
tests.code:
rm = ReloadableModule()
rm.install('demo')
rm.simulate_body_execution('demo')
m1 = rm.import_again('demo')
m2 = rm.import_again('demo')
m3 = rm.import_again('demo')
assert m1 is m2 is m3, 'import must return the same module object'
assert m1.exec_count == 1, f'exec_count: {m1.exec_count}'
assert rm.identity_stable('demo')
print('ok')
tests.hint: sys.modules[name] is the cache: import_again is a dict lookup, nothing executes.
